summary: Fidelity audit addendum: the PolicyConfig closure must also preflight maxRegisteredEntities before relational/math operators and must default exported evaluatePolicy config only on exact nil. Current PR #274 head 5251998df21e8f7f78cae5c046d346496cc65a28 can execute hostile relational metamethods from a plain config whose maxRegisteredEntities is a table, because validateConfig evaluates >=, <, and math.floor before a primitive-number guard. Separately, evaluatePolicy uses config or DEFAULT_CONFIG, so explicit false silently selects defaults instead of failing closed. These are part of the same no-execute/malformed-input boundary already blocking PR #274, not new feature work; PR #325 has been asked to extend its adversarial proof accordingly.
evidence: PR #274 audit addendum review 4904336152 records both cases on exact head 5251998df21e8f7f78cae5c046d346496cc65a28.
PR #325 audit review 4904334272 requests adversarial regressions for hostile maxRegisteredEntities and explicit false config.
FidelityManager.validateConfig begins with maxRegisteredEntities relational/math operators before any type guard for that field.
FidelityManager.evaluatePolicy currently resolves config with `config or DEFAULT_CONFIG`, making explicit false indistinguishable from omitted nil at runtime.
